tickerText: [TENNIS] Wimbledon 2026 Day 10 Thursday, July 9: British wildcard Arthur Fery completed a fairy-tale run on Wednesday, dismantling Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 7-6 (7-4), 6-0 on Centre Court to become only the fifth British man in the Open era to reach a Wimbledon semi-final — he faces French Open champion Alexander Zverev on Friday after the German beat Taylor Fritz 6-4, 6-4, 6-2 • Friday's blockbuster men's semi-finals open with Novak Djokovic vs defending champion Jannik Sinner at 1:30pm BST on Centre Court, with Fery-Zverev to follow — Djokovic still recovering from his record 5-hour-15-minute quarter-final epic over Felix Auger-Aliassime • Thursday's women's semis: Coco Gauff meets Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova faces Marta Kostyuk, with a first-time Wimbledon champion guaranteed after Iga Swiatek and Aryna Sabalenka fell earlier in the draw • [SQUASH] The 2025-26 PSA Squash Tour season closed in June with Diego Elias becoming the first South American to win the PSA Tour Finals and Hania El Hammamy beating Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam for her second Finals crown — attention now shifts to the 2026-27 campaign starting in August, while Mohammad Syafiq Kamal and India's Tanvi Khanna carry Mumbai Challenger momentum into the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games buildup • [BADMINTON] The DAIHATSU Japan Open Super 750 fires up July 14–19 at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium with a $950,000 purse — Malaysia's scratch men's doubles pair Man Wei Chong and Olympic bronze medallist Soh Wooi Yik open against Taiwan's Lee brothers, Indonesia fields 12 players led by Jonatan Christie and three men's doubles pairs, and BAM's new AI Instant Review System from the AFFIN 100PLUS Junior Elite Tour Finals heads to Singapore in August • [PICKLEBALL] Hong Kit Wong captured his third PPA Tour Asia singles title at the Sansan Tokyo Open without dropping a game, beating Australia's Mitchell Hargreaves in the final as Hargreaves jumped 15 spots to No. 24 in the rankings — Tama Shimabukuro took men's doubles and mixed doubles gold in Tokyo, and the Leapmotor PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open arrives July 23–26 at The Sports Arina @ Expo with a $70,000 purse • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT United States Smash 2026 concluded Sunday in Ontario, California — Sun Yingsha edged Kuai Man 4-3 in a seven-game women's final for her sixth career Grand Smash title, Japan's Sora Matsushima won men's singles after China's Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong were both ousted in the round of 16, and the circuit rolls on to WTT Star Contender Brazil July 21–26 in São José dos Campos

newsItems.title: Syafiq Kamal's Mumbai Comeback Secures Asian Games Squad Spot
newsItems.excerpt: Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal produced one of the comebacks of the early summer squash season at the HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger Tour Mumbai 2026, fighting back from two games down to defeat Egypt's second seed Yassin Shohdy 6-11, 9-11, 11-8, 14-12, 11-8 in a gripping men's final at the Juhu Gymkhana Club. The victory ended a seven-year drought since Syafiq's last PSA crown and arrived with extra significance after the Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia confirmed his place in the national squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games from September 19 to October 4. Shohdy had controlled the opening two games and looked poised to add to his ACE Challenger triumph in Kerteh, but Syafiq raised his intensity to force a decider and closed with an 11-8 fifth-game win. The women's final delivered equal drama as India's Tanvi Khanna, the world No. 74 and third seed, recovered from 0-2 down to beat Egyptian second seed Farida Walid 8-11, 2-11, 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 for her fifth PSA title in 11 final appearances. The five-day event featured 48 professionals from 15 countries and underscored India's growing profile on the global PSA calendar as the 2026-27 season prepares to launch in August.

newsItems.title: Wei Chong and Wooi Yik Launch New Malaysia Doubles Era at Japan Open
newsItems.excerpt: The DAIHATSU Japan Open, a BWF World Tour Super 750 event with a $950,000 prize purse, begins July 14 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium and will mark the competitive debut of Malaysia's reshuffled men's doubles pairing of Man Wei Chong and Olympic bronze medallist Soh Wooi Yik. National coach Herry IP has been testing several new combinations ahead of the Asian Games cycle, and the scratch pair face a demanding opener against Taiwan's world No. 18 duo Lee Fang Chih and Lee Fang Jen, with a potential second-round clash against either France's Popov brothers or Indonesia's second seeds Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri awaiting the winner. Indonesia has confirmed a 12-player delegation across all disciplines, leaning on three men's doubles pairs as its primary strength, while Jonatan Christie and Alwi Farhan lead the singles charge. The tournament arrives days after the Badminton Association of Malaysia became the first body in the region to deploy an AI-powered Instant Review System at the AFFIN 100PLUS Junior Elite Tour Finals, with Revealtek's BWF-approved technology set to expand to the Singapore International Challenge in August.

newsItems.title: Hong Kit Wong Dominates Tokyo Open for Third PPA Asia Singles Crown
newsItems.excerpt: Hong Kit Wong extended his remarkable run on the PPA Tour Asia circuit by capturing his third singles title at the Sansan Tokyo Open without dropping a game, defeating Australia's Mitchell Hargreaves in the final after eliminating top seed Zane Ford in the semi-finals. Wong, who also won the Capital Securities Beijing Open three weeks earlier, has climbed to No. 15 on the PPA singles rankings despite focusing exclusively on the Asian tour. Hargreaves enjoyed the biggest ranking jump among the highlighted players, moving up 15 positions to No. 24 after his silver-medal run through the bottom half of the draw. Tama Shimabukuro was another Tokyo standout, claiming both the men's doubles and mixed doubles titles and climbing seven places to World No. 14 in mixed doubles, while Sahra Dennehy and Rika Fujiwara also posted significant ranking gains. Attention now turns to the Leapmotor PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open from July 23 to 26 at The Sports Arina @ Expo, the first PPA Tour Asia event staged in Singapore, with registrations also open for the Shenzhen Open in August and the $1.1 million Hong Kong Slam in October.

newsItems.title: Sun Yingsha Claims Sixth Grand Smash Title at WTT U.S. Smash
newsItems.excerpt: Sun Yingsha added another milestone to her dominant 2026 season by edging compatriot Kuai Man 4-3 in an all-China women's singles final at the WTT United States Smash in Ontario, California, prevailing 11-9, 11-6, 9-11, 11-5, 7-11, 10-12, 11-4 to claim her sixth career Grand Smash title and second of the year. The 25-year-old world champion said staying focused through the deciding game represented a major step forward, while Kuai reflected on a breakthrough run that included doubles gold alongside Wang Manyu. On the men's side, Japan's Sora Matsushima captured singles gold after a tournament that saw defending champion Wang Chuqin eliminated by Denmark's Anders Lind in the round of 16 and Lin Shidong fall to France's Alexis Lebrun, ending China's men's singles campaign before the quarter-finals. China still swept both doubles titles as Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen won men's doubles and Wang Manyu and Kuai Man took the women's crown. The World Table Tennis calendar now shifts to the WTT Star Contender Brazil from July 21 to 26 in São José dos Campos, where home hope Hugo Calderano and more than 80 international players will compete for a $300,000 prize pool.
